title: Beneath the Hill
text:
In the moonlight, that hill
seemed to sway,
like a great sailing boat
unable to move forward,
caught in a predicament.

How much history it must have seen—
war, love, birth, death, kingdoms, anarchy;
how much creation and destruction
it must have witnessed.
Since the day I heard it existed,
the wish to see it
had flowed like a river through burning desert sand.

Fighting for a throne,
the greater part of my life was laid waste.
Was it real, or imagined?
Even now I cannot tell.
Blood runs from my body;
my breaths have lost their way.

After a whirlwind
flung me here, it began to show, faintly.
At first it seemed an illusion,
perhaps the remains of uncertainty
someone had served up for me.

Is this the shape of my hunger?
Has it risen from my meditation?
Is it the ghost of my failure?
Is it the messenger of my death?
For a while, a bed of questions.

Did it come closer,
or did I crawl towards it?
Now I can see it,
my eyes brimming.

How far away?
It seems so close.
The illusion has not lifted.

The hill sways; perhaps
at my touch it will sail away,
and I with it,
taking with me
my dreams, truth, lies, history,
and leaving for you
a vast, empty plain.
